source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's emphatic denial and divine commissioning.
verses.before: Paul, an apostle—not from human beings or through a human being, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised him from the dead—
verses.after: Paul, an apostle—not from human beings nor through a human being, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead—
verses.tsw_comparator: Paul, an apostle—not from human beings nor through a human, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead—

verses.rationale: Keeps the co-senders and multiple regional churches.
verses.before: and all the brothers and sisters with me, to the churches of Galatia:
verses.after: and all the brothers and sisters with me, to the churches of Galatia:
verses.tsw_comparator: and all the brothers and sisters who are with me, To the churches of Galatia:

verses.rationale: Retains both gifts and their source.
verses.before: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.after: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.tsw_comparator: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,

verses.rationale: Preserves self-giving, rescue, temporal evil, and divine will.
verses.before: who gave himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
verses.after: who gave himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
verses.tsw_comparator: who gave himself for our sins to deliver us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,

verses.rationale: Keeps the doxology and emphatic duration.
verses.before: to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.after: to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.tsw_comparator: to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

verses.rationale: Preserves surprise, personal desertion, grace, and interrupted clause.
verses.before: I am amazed that you are turning so quickly from the one who called you by Christ’s grace to a different good news—
verses.after: I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting the one who called you by Christ's grace and turning to a different gospel—
verses.tsw_comparator: I am astonished that you are so quickly turning away from the one who called you in the grace of Christ to a different good news—

verses.rationale: Keeps the correction and identifies human agents.
verses.before: not that there is another one. Rather, some people are troubling you and want to distort the good news of Christ.
verses.after: not that there is another gospel. But some people are troubling you and want to distort the gospel of Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: which is not another; only there are some who are troubling you and wanting to distort the good news of Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves universal condition and severe curse.
verses.before: But even if we or an angel from heaven should announce to you a good news contrary to what we announced to you, let that one be under a curse.
verses.after: But even if we or an angel from heaven should proclaim to you a gospel contrary to the one we proclaimed to you, let that one be accursed!
verses.tsw_comparator: But even if we or an angel from heaven should proclaim to you a good news contrary to the one we proclaimed to you, let him be accursed.

verses.rationale: Keeps deliberate repetition and received message.
verses.before: As we have said before, I now say again: if anyone announces to you a good news contrary to what you received, let that one be under a curse.
verses.after: As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone proclaims to you a gospel contrary to what you received, let that one be accursed!
verses.tsw_comparator: As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone proclaims to you a good news contrary to what you received, let him be accursed.

verses.rationale: Preserves rhetorical questions and servant allegiance.
verses.before: Am I now trying to win human approval or God’s? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I would not be Christ’s servant.
verses.after: Am I now seeking human approval, or God's? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be Christ's servant.
verses.tsw_comparator: For am I now seeking the approval of human beings, or of God? Or am I trying to please human beings? If I were still pleasing human beings, I would not be a servant of Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps disclosure and source denial.
verses.before: I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that the good news I announced is not of human origin.
verses.after: For I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that the gospel proclaimed by me is not of human origin.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I make known to you, brothers and sisters, that the good news that was proclaimed by me is not according to a human source;

verses.rationale: Preserves both denials and revelation's possible source/content relation.
verses.before: I did not receive it from a human being, nor was I taught it; I received it through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.after: For I neither received it from a human being nor was I taught it; rather, I received it through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: for I did not receive it from a human, nor was I taught it, but I received it through a revelation of Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Names Paul's former religious setting and actual violence.
verses.before: You have heard about my former way of life in Judaism: how intensely I persecuted God’s church and tried to destroy it.
verses.after: For you have heard about my former way of life in Judaism: I intensely persecuted God's church and tried to destroy it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how I persecuted the church of God beyond measure and tried to destroy it,

verses.rationale: Keeps comparison, kinship, and ancestral zeal.
verses.before: I was advancing in Judaism beyond many people my own age among my people, being far more zealous for the traditions of my ancestors.
verses.after: I advanced in Judaism beyond many contemporaries among my people, being far more zealous for my ancestral traditions.
verses.tsw_comparator: and I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my people, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my ancestors.

verses.rationale: Preserves prophetic calling language and suspended sentence.
verses.before: But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me through his grace, was pleased
verses.after: But when God, who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me through his grace, was pleased
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the one who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me through his grace was pleased

verses.rationale: Keeps inward/through-me ambiguity and mission purpose.
verses.before: to reveal his Son in me so that I might announce the good news about him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult flesh and blood,
verses.after: to reveal his Son in me so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult flesh and blood,
verses.tsw_comparator: to reveal his Son in me, so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood,

verses.rationale: Preserves chronology and all locations.
verses.before: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went away to Arabia and then returned to Damascus.
verses.after: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went away to Arabia and then returned to Damascus.
verses.tsw_comparator: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia, and again returned to Damascus.

verses.rationale: Keeps source-form Cephas and exact durations.
verses.before: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to get acquainted with Cephas and stayed with him fifteen days.
verses.after: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to get acquainted with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas and remained with him fifteen days;

verses.rationale: Preserves the exception and specific relationship.
verses.before: I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.
verses.after: I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord's brother.
verses.tsw_comparator: but I saw none of the other apostles except James, the brother of the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps solemn direct assertion.
verses.before: As for what I am writing to you—look, before God, I am not lying.
verses.after: As for what I am writing to you—look, before God, I am not lying.
verses.tsw_comparator: (In what I am writing to you, before God, I am not lying.)

verses.rationale: Preserves geographic movement.
verses.before: Afterward I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
verses.after: Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

verses.rationale: Keeps facial unfamiliarity and location.
verses.before: I was still unknown by sight to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
verses.after: I was still unknown by sight to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I was still unknown by face to the churches of Judea that are in Christ;

verses.rationale: Preserves reported speech and reversal.
verses.before: They only kept hearing, “The man who once persecuted us is now announcing the faith he once tried to destroy.”
verses.after: They only kept hearing, “The man who once persecuted us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy.”
verses.tsw_comparator: they only were hearing, “The one who once persecuted us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy.”

verses.rationale: Keeps God as object and Paul as occasion.
verses.before: And they glorified God because of me.
verses.after: And they glorified God because of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they glorified God because of me.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact time, destination, and companions.
verses.before: Then after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along too.
verses.after: Then, after fourteen years, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also.

verses.rationale: Keeps revelation, public mission, private consultation, and race image.
verses.before: I went up because of a revelation and set before them the good news I proclaim among the Gentiles—but privately before those considered leaders—to make sure I was not running, or had not run, in vain.
verses.after: I went up because of a revelation and set before them the gospel I proclaim among the Gentiles—but privately before those considered influential—so that I would not be running, or have run, in vain.
verses.tsw_comparator: I went up according to a revelation and set before them the good news that I proclaim among the Gentiles—but privately before those who seemed influential—lest somehow I might be running or had run in vain.

verses.rationale: Preserves ethnicity and absence of compulsion.
verses.before: Yet even Titus, who was with me and was Greek, was not compelled to be circumcised.
verses.after: Yet even Titus, who was with me and was Greek, was not compelled to be circumcised.
verses.tsw_comparator: But not even Titus, who was with me, though he was a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.

verses.rationale: Keeps infiltration, surveillance, freedom, and enslavement.
verses.before: The issue arose because of false brothers who had slipped in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might enslave us.
verses.after: The issue arose because of false brothers who slipped in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might enslave us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet because of false brothers secretly brought in—who slipped in to spy out our freedom that we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might enslave us—

verses.rationale: Preserves resistance, duration, and protective purpose.
verses.before: We did not yield to them in submission even for an hour, so that the truth of the good news might remain with you.
verses.after: We did not yield to them in submission even for an hour, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: to them we did not yield in submission even for a moment, so that the truth of the good news might remain with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's dismissive parenthesis and nonpartiality.
verses.before: As for those who were considered important—whatever they once were makes no difference to me; God does not show partiality—they added nothing to my message.
verses.after: But from those considered influential—whatever they once were makes no difference to me; God shows no partiality—those influential people added nothing to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: And from those who seemed to be something—what they were makes no difference to me; God shows no partiality—those, I say, who seemed influential added nothing to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two mission fields and entrusted gospel.
verses.before: On the contrary, when they saw that I had been entrusted with the good news for the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been for the circumcised—
verses.after: On the contrary, when they saw that I had been entrusted with the gospel for the uncircumcised, just as Peter had for the circumcised—
verses.tsw_comparator: On the contrary, when they saw that I had been entrusted with the good news to the uncircumcised, just as Peter to the circumcised

verses.rationale: Keeps shared divine agency and distinct missions.
verses.before: for the one who worked through Peter for apostleship among the circumcised also worked through me among the Gentiles—
verses.after: for the one who worked through Peter for an apostleship to the circumcised also worked through me for the Gentiles—
verses.tsw_comparator: (for the one who worked through Peter for the apostleship to the circumcised also worked through me for the Gentiles),

verses.rationale: Preserves names, perceived status, recognition, agreement, and destinations.
verses.before: and when James, Cephas, and John, who were considered pillars, recognized the grace given to me, they gave Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship, agreeing that we should go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised.
verses.after: and when James, Cephas, and John, who were considered pillars, recognized the grace given to me, they gave Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship: we would go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
verses.tsw_comparator: and when James and Cephas and John, who were regarded as pillars, perceived the grace that had been given to me, they gave to Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship, that we should go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised—

verses.rationale: Keeps the sole request and Paul's eagerness.
verses.before: They asked only that we remember the poor—the very thing I was eager to do.
verses.after: They asked only that we remember the poor—the very thing I was also eager to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: only they asked us to remember the poor, which very thing I was eager to do.

verses.rationale: Preserves source name, place, public confrontation, and judgment.
verses.before: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face because he stood condemned.
verses.after: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.

verses.rationale: Keeps chronology, table fellowship, withdrawal, and fear.
verses.before: Before certain people came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they came, he drew back and separated himself because he was afraid of those from the circumcision group.
verses.after: For before certain people came from James, he used to eat with Gentiles. But when they came, he drew back and separated himself because he feared those of the circumcision.
verses.tsw_comparator: For before certain men came from James, he was eating with the Gentiles; but when they came, he drew back and separated himself, fearing those of the circumcision.

verses.rationale: Preserves group identities and hypocrisy's influence.
verses.before: The rest of the Jewish believers joined him in this hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was led astray by their hypocrisy.
verses.after: And the rest of the Jews joined him in hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was led astray by their hypocrisy.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the rest of the Jews joined him in hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.

verses.rationale: Keeps public rebuke, identities, conduct, and coercion question.
verses.before: But when I saw that they were not walking straight according to the truth of the good news, I said to Cephas in front of everyone, “If you, though Jewish, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
verses.after: But when I saw that they were not walking straight according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of everyone, “If you, though a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when I saw that they were not walking straight according to the truth of the good news, I said to Cephas before them all, “If you, though a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's insider formulation while quotation marks signal the contested label.
verses.before: We are Jews by birth and not sinners from among the Gentiles,
verses.after: We are Jews by birth and not “Gentile sinners,”
verses.tsw_comparator: We ourselves are Jews by birth and not Gentile sinners;

verses.rationale: Preserves all repetitions and renders the genitive as Christ's faithfulness while noting human believing.
verses.before: yet we know that a person is not set right by works of the Law but through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ. So we too have trusted in Christ Jesus so that we might be set right through the faithfulness of Christ and not by works of the Law, because by works of the Law no flesh will be set right.
verses.after: yet we know that a person is not justified by works of the law but through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ. So we too believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by Christ's faithfulness and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no flesh will be justified.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet we know that a person is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ. And we have believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no flesh will be justified.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional objection and forceful denial.
verses.before: But if, while seeking to be set right in Christ, we ourselves were found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? Certainly not!
verses.after: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, does that make Christ a servant of sin? Absolutely not!
verses.tsw_comparator: But if, in seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? Certainly not!

verses.rationale: Preserves construction metaphor and self-indictment.
verses.before: For if I rebuild what I tore down, I prove myself a transgressor.
verses.after: For if I rebuild what I tore down, I demonstrate that I am a transgressor.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if I build up again the things I once tore down, I prove myself to be a transgressor.

verses.rationale: Keeps paradox, purpose, and co-crucifixion.
verses.before: Through the Law I died to the Law so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ.
verses.after: For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God.

verses.rationale: Preserves embodied life and again renders the genitive as the Son's faithfulness.
verses.before: It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh, I live by the faithfulness of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
verses.after: It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the flesh, I live by the faithfulness of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have been crucified with Christ; and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the stark consequence.
verses.before: I do not set aside God’s grace, because if righteousness comes through the Law, then Christ died for nothing.
verses.after: I do not set aside God's grace, for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.

verses.rationale: Retains direct rebuke, bewitching image, and public portrayal.
verses.before: Foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified.
verses.after: O foolish Galatians! Who bewitched you? Before your eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified.
verses.tsw_comparator: O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified?

verses.rationale: Keeps the single diagnostic question and contrast.
verses.before: I want to learn only this from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the Law or by hearing with trust?
verses.after: I want to learn only this from you: did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
verses.tsw_comparator: Let me ask you only this: did you receive the Spirit by works of the law or by hearing with faith?

verses.rationale: Preserves beginning/completion and Spirit/flesh contrasts.
verses.before: Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being brought to completion by the flesh?
verses.after: Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being completed by the flesh?
verses.tsw_comparator: Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being completed by the flesh?

verses.rationale: Keeps the verb's suffer/experience range and final qualification.
verses.before: Did you experience so much for nothing—if indeed it was for nothing?
verses.after: Did you experience so much in vain—if it really was in vain?
verses.tsw_comparator: Did you suffer so many things in vain—if indeed it was in vain?

verses.rationale: Preserves present divine action and repeated contrast.
verses.before: So then, does the one who supplies the Spirit to you and works miracles among you do so by works of the Law or by hearing with trust?
verses.after: So does the one who supplies the Spirit to you and works miracles among you do so by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then does the one who supplies the Spirit to you and works miracles among you do so by works of the law or by hearing with faith?

verses.rationale: Keeps the scriptural wording and accounting image.
verses.before: Just as Abraham trusted God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
verses.after: Just as “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Just as Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness,

verses.rationale: Preserves kinship claim without male-only English.
verses.before: Know, then, that those who live by trust are Abraham’s children.
verses.after: Know, then, that those who belong to faith are Abraham's children.
verses.tsw_comparator: know then that those of faith—these are sons of Abraham.

verses.rationale: Keeps Scripture personified and promise scope.
verses.before: Scripture, foreseeing that God would set the Gentiles right by trust, announced the good news beforehand to Abraham: “All the nations will be blessed in you.”
verses.after: And Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, announced the gospel beforehand to Abraham: “All the nations will be blessed in you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, proclaimed the good news beforehand to Abraham, saying, “In you shall all the nations be blessed.”

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated faith word and shared blessing.
verses.before: So those who live by trust are blessed with Abraham, the one who trusted.
verses.after: So those who belong to faith are blessed together with faithful Abraham.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then, those of faith are blessed along with Abraham, the one who believed.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal scope and full quotation demand.
verses.before: For all who rely on works of the Law are under a curse, because it is written, “Cursed is everyone who does not continue in everything written in the book of the Law, to do it.”
verses.after: For all who rely on works of the law are under a curse, because it is written, “Cursed is everyone who does not continue in everything written in the book of the law, to do it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For all who are of works of the law are under a curse; for it is written, “Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all things written in the book of the law, to do them.”

verses.rationale: Preserves conclusion and scriptural reason.
verses.before: Now it is clear that no one is set right before God by the Law, because “the righteous one will live by trust.”
verses.after: Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, because “the righteous one will live by faith.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the law, for “the righteous one shall live by faith.”

verses.rationale: Keeps contrast and quotation.
verses.before: But the Law is not based on trust; rather, “the one who does these things will live by them.”
verses.after: But the law does not operate by faith; instead, “The one who does these things will live by them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the law is not of faith; rather, “the one who does them shall live by them.”

verses.rationale: Preserves redemption, substitution, curse, and tree image.
verses.before: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law by becoming a curse for us, because it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree,”
verses.after: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, because it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree,”
verses.tsw_comparator: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us—for it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree”—

verses.rationale: Keeps double purpose and promise.
verses.before: so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that we might receive the promised Spirit through trust.
verses.after: so that in Christ Jesus Abraham's blessing might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

verses.rationale: Preserves human analogy and legal actions.
verses.before: Brothers and sisters, I am speaking in human terms: even with a human covenant, once it has been ratified, no one sets it aside or adds to it.
verses.after: Brothers and sisters, I speak in human terms: even a human covenant, once ratified, cannot be annulled or supplemented by anyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Brothers and sisters, I speak according to human terms: even a human covenant, once ratified, no one sets aside or adds to it.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's singular/plural argument and collective wordplay.
verses.before: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring. It does not say, “and to offsprings,” as though referring to many, but to one: “and to your offspring,” who is Christ.
verses.after: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring. It does not say, “and to offsprings,” as referring to many, but as to one: “and to your offspring,” who is Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring. It does not say, “And to offsprings,” as of many, but as of one, “And to your offspring,” who is Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact number, chronology, and legal consequence.
verses.before: What I mean is this: the Law, which came four hundred thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously established by God so as to cancel the promise.
verses.after: What I mean is this: the law, which came four hundred thirty years later, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God and so cancel the promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what I mean: the law, which came four hundred thirty years afterward, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise.

verses.rationale: Keeps inheritance contrast and grace verb.
verses.before: For if the inheritance comes from the Law, it no longer comes from promise. But God graciously gave it to Abraham through a promise.
verses.after: For if the inheritance comes by the law, it no longer comes by promise. But God graciously gave it to Abraham through a promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if the inheritance is from the law, it is no longer from promise; but God has given it to Abraham through a promise.

verses.rationale: Preserves purpose ambiguity, duration, angels, and mediator.
verses.before: Why then the Law? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise had been made. It was put in place through angels by the hand of a mediator.
verses.after: Why, then, the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring to whom the promise had been made would come. It was arranged through angels by the hand of a mediator.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why then the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise had been made, having been ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.

verses.rationale: Keeps the compressed and difficult contrast.
verses.before: Now a mediator is not for one party only, but God is one.
verses.after: Now a mediator is not for one party alone, but God is one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now a mediator is not for one alone, but God is one.

verses.rationale: Preserves question, denial, and unreal condition.
verses.before: Is the Law then opposed to God’s promises? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could give life, righteousness would indeed come from the Law.
verses.after: Is the law, then, opposed to God's promises? Absolutely not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, righteousness would indeed have come by the law.
verses.tsw_comparator: Is the law then against the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that was able to give life, then righteousness would indeed be from the law.

verses.rationale: Keeps confinement image, universal scope, Christ's faithfulness, and believing recipients.
verses.before: But Scripture imprisoned everything under sin so that the promise through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ might be given to those who trust.
verses.after: But Scripture imprisoned everything under sin, so that the promise by the faithfulness of Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Scripture imprisoned all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.

verses.rationale: Preserves guarded imprisonment and temporal movement.
verses.before: Before this trust came, we were kept under the Law, imprisoned until the trust that was about to be revealed.
verses.after: Before this faith came, we were held under guard by the law, imprisoned until the coming faith would be revealed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But before faith came, we were held in custody under the law, imprisoned until the coming faith was to be revealed.

verses.rationale: Renders the household supervisor rather than modern classroom teacher.
verses.before: So the Law became our guardian until Christ, so that we might be set right by trust.
verses.after: Thus the law became our guardian until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then, the law has become our guardian until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.

verses.rationale: Keeps temporal conclusion and household image.
verses.before: But now that this trust has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
verses.after: But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.

verses.rationale: Retains the gendered inheritance status of sons while addressing all.
verses.before: For all of you are God’s children through trust in Christ Jesus.
verses.after: For all of you are God's sons through faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.

verses.rationale: Keeps baptism and clothing image.
verses.before: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
verses.after: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves actual enslaved status, creation echo, and unity.
verses.before: There is no Jew or Greek, slave or free, male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
verses.after: There is no Jew or Greek, there is no enslaved or free person, there is no male and female, for all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no Jew or Greek, there is no slave or free, there is no male and female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.

verses.rationale: Keeps belonging, kinship, and inheritance.
verses.before: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s offspring, heirs according to promise.
verses.after: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s offspring, heirs according to the promise.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancient household status, gendered heir, and paradox.
verses.before: What I mean is this: as long as an heir is a child, that heir differs in no way from a slave, though being owner of everything.
verses.after: What I mean is that as long as an heir is a minor, he differs in no way from an enslaved person, though he is owner of everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: I mean this: as long as an heir is a child, the heir differs in no way from a slave, though the heir is the owner of everything.

verses.rationale: Keeps household roles and paternal deadline.
verses.before: Instead, the heir is under guardians and managers until the date set by the father.
verses.after: Instead, he is under guardians and estate managers until the date set by his father.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rather, the heir is under guardians and stewards until the date set by the father.

verses.rationale: Retains real enslavement and the ambiguous cosmic elements/powers.
verses.before: In the same way, when we were children, we were enslaved under the elemental powers of the world.
verses.after: In the same way, when we were minors, we were enslaved under the elemental powers of the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: So also we, when we were children, were enslaved under the elemental powers of the world.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine sending, human birth, and legal location.
verses.before: But when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the Law,
verses.after: But when the fullness of time came, God sent out his Son, born from a woman, born under the law,
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent the Son, born of a woman, born under the law,

verses.rationale: Preserves release and gendered inheritance status.
verses.before: to redeem those under the Law so that we might receive adoption as sons and daughters.
verses.after: to redeem those under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children.

verses.rationale: Keeps shift from you to our, Spirit's cry, and Aramaic address.
verses.before: And because you are sons and daughters, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba! Father!”
verses.after: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba, Father!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of the Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba! Father!”

verses.rationale: Preserves singular address and status change.
verses.before: So you are no longer a slave but a child; and if a child, then also an heir through God.
verses.after: So you are no longer enslaved but a son; and if a son, then also an heir through God.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you are no longer a slave but a child, and if a child, then also an heir through God.

verses.rationale: Keeps past condition and denial of divine nature.
verses.before: Formerly, when you did not know God, you were enslaved to beings that by nature are not gods.
verses.after: But formerly, when you did not know God, you were enslaved to beings that by nature are not gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: Formerly, when you did not know God, you were enslaved to those that by nature are not gods.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's correction and renewed enslavement question.
verses.before: But now that you know God—or rather, are known by God—how can you turn back again to the weak and poor elemental powers? Do you want to be enslaved to them all over again?
verses.after: But now that you know God—or rather, are known by God—how can you turn back again to the weak and impoverished elemental powers? Do you want to be enslaved to them all over again?
verses.tsw_comparator: But now that you have come to know God—or rather to be known by God—how can you turn back again to the weak and impoverished elemental powers, whose slaves you want to be once more?

verses.rationale: Keeps the fourfold calendar list.
verses.before: You carefully observe days, months, seasons, and years.
verses.after: You carefully observe days and months and seasons and years.
verses.tsw_comparator: You observe days and months and seasons and years!

verses.rationale: Preserves relational fear and labor.
verses.before: I am afraid for you, that perhaps I have labored over you in vain.
verses.after: I fear for you that perhaps I have labored over you in vain.
verses.tsw_comparator: I fear for you, that perhaps I have labored over you in vain.

verses.rationale: Keeps mutual identification, appeal, and transition.
verses.before: I beg you, brothers and sisters: become as I am, because I became as you are. You did me no wrong.
verses.after: Become as I am, because I also became as you are, brothers and sisters—I plead with you. You did me no wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Become as I am, for I also have become as you are, brothers and sisters. You did me no wrong.

verses.rationale: Names bodily weakness without diagnosing it.
verses.before: You know that it was because of a bodily weakness that I first announced the good news to you.
verses.after: You know that it was because of a bodily weakness that I first proclaimed the gospel to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You know that it was because of a weakness of the flesh that I proclaimed the good news to you the first time,

verses.rationale: Keeps disability-like stigma, rejection verbs, and extraordinary welcome.
verses.before: Though my bodily condition was a trial for you, you did not despise or reject me. Instead, you received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
verses.after: Although my bodily condition was a trial for you, you did not despise or spit at me. Instead, you welcomed me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: and though my condition was a trial to you, you did not despise or reject me, but received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus himself.

verses.rationale: Retains violent hyperbole without inferring an eye illness.
verses.before: Where then is the blessedness you had? I testify that, if possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
verses.after: Where, then, is that sense of blessing you had? For I testify that, if possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Where then is that blessing of yours? For I testify to you that, if possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct relational question.
verses.before: So have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
verses.after: So have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
verses.tsw_comparator: So have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?

verses.rationale: Preserves manipulation through exclusion and attention.
verses.before: Those people are eager for you, but not for a good purpose. They want to shut you out so that you will be eager for them.
verses.after: Those people are zealous for you, but not for a good purpose. They want to shut you out so that you will be zealous for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are eager for you, but not for good; they want to shut you out, so that you may be eager for them.

verses.rationale: Keeps wordplay and presence contrast.
verses.before: It is good to be eagerly sought for a good purpose always, and not only when I am present with you.
verses.after: Now it is good to be sought eagerly for a good purpose at all times, and not only when I am present with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is always good to be sought eagerly for a good purpose—and not only when I am present with you.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's maternal birth image and unfinished sentence.
verses.before: My children, for whom I am again suffering birth pains until Christ is formed in you,
verses.after: My children, for whom I am again in labor pains until Christ is formed in you,
verses.tsw_comparator: My little children, for whom I am again in the pain of childbirth until Christ is formed in you,

verses.rationale: Keeps desire, vocal change, and uncertainty.
verses.before: I wish I could be present with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.
verses.after: I wish I could be present with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I wish I could be present with you now and change my tone, for I am perplexed about you.

verses.rationale: Preserves law's two senses and challenging question.
verses.before: Tell me, you who want to be under the Law: do you not listen to the Law?
verses.after: Tell me, you who want to be under the law: do you not listen to the law?
verses.tsw_comparator: Tell me, you who desire to be under the law, do you not listen to the law?

verses.rationale: Retains gender and actual enslaved/free status.
verses.before: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and one by the free woman.
verses.after: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the enslaved woman and one by the free woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman and one by a free woman.

verses.rationale: Keeps birth and promise contrast.
verses.before: But the son of the slave woman was born according to the flesh, while the son of the free woman was born through promise.
verses.after: The one by the enslaved woman was born according to the flesh, but the one by the free woman through promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the son of the slave was born according to the flesh, while the son of the free woman was born through promise.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's stated allegory, geography, and slavery.
verses.before: These things are being spoken allegorically, for these women are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children for slavery; this is Hagar.
verses.after: These things are being interpreted allegorically, for these women represent two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children into slavery; this is Hagar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now this may be interpreted allegorically: these women are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children for slavery; she is Hagar.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult identification, location, and correspondence.
verses.before: Now Hagar corresponds to Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, because she is in slavery with her children.
verses.after: Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is enslaved with her children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.

verses.rationale: Preserves female city image and kinship.
verses.before: But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
verses.after: But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.

verses.rationale: Keeps all gendered imagery and comparative quotation.
verses.before: For it is written, “Rejoice, barren woman who does not bear; break out and cry aloud, you who are not in labor, because the children of the deserted woman are more numerous than those of the woman who has a husband.”
verses.after: For it is written, “Rejoice, barren woman who does not give birth; break out and cry aloud, woman who has no labor pains, because the deserted woman's children are more numerous than those of the woman who has a husband.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is written, “Rejoice, O barren one who does not bear; break forth and cry aloud, you who are not in labor; for the children of the desolate one are more than those of the one who has a husband.”

verses.rationale: Preserves community's comparison with Isaac.
verses.before: Now you, brothers and sisters, like Isaac, are children of promise.
verses.after: Now you, brothers and sisters, are children of promise, like Isaac.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now you, brothers and sisters, like Isaac, are children of promise.

verses.rationale: Keeps persecution and temporal analogy.
verses.before: But just as the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit then, so it is now.
verses.after: But just as then the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, so it is now.
verses.tsw_comparator: But just as at that time the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, so it is now also.

verses.rationale: Retains the harsh expulsion quotation and status terms.
verses.before: But what does the Scripture say? “Drive out the slave woman and her son, because the slave woman’s son will certainly not inherit with the free woman’s son.”
verses.after: But what does Scripture say? “Drive out the enslaved woman and her son, for the son of the enslaved woman will certainly not inherit with the son of the free woman.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But what does the scripture say? “Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave shall not inherit with the son of the free woman.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the allegorical conclusion and community identity.
verses.before: Therefore, brothers and sisters, we are not children of the slave woman but of the free woman.
verses.after: Therefore, brothers and sisters, we are not children of the enslaved woman, but of the free woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then, brothers and sisters, we are not children of the slave but of the free woman.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic freedom, command, and yoke image.
verses.before: For freedom Christ set us free. Therefore stand firm and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
verses.after: For freedom Christ set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not be held again under a yoke of slavery.
verses.tsw_comparator: For freedom Christ has set us free; stand fast therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.

verses.rationale: Keeps personal emphasis and conditional warning.
verses.before: Look—I, Paul, tell you that if you are circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
verses.after: Look, I, Paul, tell you that if you are circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I, Paul, say to you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you.

verses.rationale: Retains male specificity and total obligation.
verses.before: Again I testify to every man who is circumcised that he is obligated to keep the whole Law.
verses.after: Again I testify to every man who is circumcised that he is obligated to do the whole law.
verses.tsw_comparator: I testify again to every man who lets himself be circumcised that he is bound to keep the whole law.

verses.rationale: Keeps severing wordplay and grace contrast.
verses.before: You who seek to be set right by the Law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.
verses.after: You who seek to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.
verses.tsw_comparator: You who would be justified by the law are severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.

verses.rationale: Preserves Spirit, faith, hope, and waiting.
verses.before: For through the Spirit, by trust, we eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness.
verses.after: For through the Spirit, by faith, we eagerly await the hope of righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For through the Spirit, by faith, we wait for the hope of righteousness.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily statuses and active faith/love relation.
verses.before: In Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any power, but trust working through love.
verses.after: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision accomplishes anything, but faith working through love does.
verses.tsw_comparator: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but faith working through love.

verses.rationale: Preserves race image and personal interference.
verses.before: You were running well. Who cut in on you and kept you from obeying the truth?
verses.after: You were running well. Who cut in on you and kept you from obeying the truth?
verses.tsw_comparator: You were running well; who hindered you from obeying the truth?

verses.rationale: Keeps calling contrast and terse judgment.
verses.before: This persuasion does not come from the one who calls you.
verses.after: That persuasion does not come from the one who calls you.
verses.tsw_comparator: This persuasion is not from the one who calls you.

verses.rationale: Retains proverbial image and total effect.
verses.before: A little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough.
verses.after: A little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough.
verses.tsw_comparator: A little leaven leavens the whole batch.

verses.rationale: Preserves confidence, anonymity, and accountability.
verses.before: I am confident about you in the Lord that you will think no differently. But the one troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever that person may be.
verses.after: I am confident about you in the Lord that you will think no differently. But the one troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever that person may be.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am confident in the Lord that you will take no other view; and the one who is troubling you will bear his judgment, whoever he is.

verses.rationale: Keeps counterfactual logic, persecution, and scandal.
verses.before: Brothers and sisters, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the offense of the cross has been removed.
verses.after: But as for me, brothers and sisters, if I still proclaim circumcision, why am I still persecuted? In that case, the offense of the cross has been abolished.
verses.tsw_comparator: But brothers and sisters, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the offense of the cross has been removed.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's harsh bodily wordplay rather than euphemizing it.
verses.before: I wish those who are unsettling you would go all the way and mutilate themselves!
verses.after: I wish those who are unsettling you would go all the way and castrate themselves!
verses.tsw_comparator: I wish that those who are unsettling you would mutilate themselves!

verses.rationale: Keeps freedom and voluntary enslavement in deliberate tension.
verses.before: For you were called to freedom, brothers and sisters. Only do not use freedom as an opportunity for the flesh; instead, through love serve one another as slaves.
verses.after: For you were called to freedom, brothers and sisters. Only do not use freedom as an opportunity for the flesh; instead, through love serve one another as enslaved people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you were called to freedom, brothers and sisters; only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.

verses.rationale: Preserves wholeness, fulfillment, and quotation.
verses.before: For the whole Law is fulfilled in one statement: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
verses.after: For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

verses.rationale: Retains violent animal imagery and reciprocal destruction.
verses.before: But if you bite and devour one another, watch out or you will be consumed by one another.
verses.after: But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement image and strong negation.
verses.before: But I say: walk by the Spirit, and you will certainly not carry out the desire of the flesh.
verses.after: But I say: walk by the Spirit, and you will certainly not carry out the desire of the flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.

verses.rationale: Preserves mutual opposition and resulting constraint.
verses.before: For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. These oppose each other so that you do not simply do whatever you want.
verses.after: For the flesh desires what is against the Spirit, and the Spirit what is against the flesh. These oppose each other, so that you do not do whatever you want.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh; for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you would.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional leadership and legal conclusion.
verses.before: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the Law.
verses.after: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.

verses.rationale: Preserves opening items and continuation.
verses.before: Now the works of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality,
verses.after: Now the works of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, debauchery,
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality,

verses.rationale: Keeps the full social and religious catalogue.
verses.before: idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambition, divisions, factions,
verses.after: idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, selfish ambitions, divisions, factions,
verses.tsw_comparator: idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, factions,

verses.rationale: Preserves continuing category, prior warning, practice, and inheritance.
verses.before: envy, drunkenness, wild parties, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who practice such things will not inherit God’s kingdom.
verses.after: envy, drunkenness, wild parties, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who practice such things will not inherit God's kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: envy, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps singular fruit and the first seven qualities.
verses.before: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
verses.after: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
verses.tsw_comparator: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

verses.rationale: Completes the list and legal conclusion.
verses.before: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
verses.after: gentleness, and self-control. There is no law against such things.
verses.tsw_comparator: gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law.

verses.rationale: Retains violent crucifixion image and embodied impulses.
verses.before: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
verses.after: Now those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
verses.tsw_comparator: And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.

verses.rationale: Keeps life and ordered-walking relation.
verses.before: If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit.
verses.after: If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit.

verses.rationale: Preserves three communal dangers and repetition.
verses.before: Let us not become conceited, provoking one another and envying one another.
verses.after: Let us not become conceited, provoking one another and envying one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us not become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another.

verses.rationale: Keeps restoration, gentleness, and self-scrutiny.
verses.before: Brothers and sisters, even if someone is caught in some wrongdoing, you who are spiritual should restore that person in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself so that you too are not tested.
verses.after: Brothers and sisters, even if someone is caught in some trespass, you who are spiritual should restore that person in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself so that you too are not tempted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Brothers and sisters, even if a person is caught in some transgression, you who are spiritual should restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself, lest you also be tempted.

verses.rationale: Preserves mutual burden-bearing and fulfillment.
verses.before: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way fulfill the law of Christ.
verses.after: Carry one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bear one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps inflated self-assessment and self-deception.
verses.before: For if anyone thinks they are something when they are nothing, they deceive themselves.
verses.after: For if anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if anyone thinks he is something, when he is nothing, he deceives himself.

verses.rationale: Preserves self-examination and noncomparative boasting.
verses.before: Each person should test their own work, and then they will have reason for satisfaction in themselves alone and not in comparison with someone else.
verses.after: But each person should test their own work, and then the reason for boasting will concern themselves alone and not the other person,
verses.tsw_comparator: But let each one examine his own work, and then he will have reason for boasting in himself alone and not in another;

verses.rationale: Keeps personal responsibility alongside shared burdens.
verses.before: For each person will carry their own load.
verses.after: for each person will carry their own load.
verses.tsw_comparator: for each will bear his own load.

verses.rationale: Preserves material/general sharing and reciprocal roles.
verses.before: The one who is taught the word should share all good things with the one who teaches.
verses.after: The one being taught the word should share every good thing with the one who teaches.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the one who is taught the word share all good things with the one who teaches.

verses.rationale: Keeps warning and sow/reap correspondence.
verses.before: Do not be deceived: God is not mocked. Whatever a person sows, that is what they will reap.
verses.after: Do not be deceived: God is not mocked. For whatever a person sows, that is also what the person will reap.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be deceived: God is not mocked, for whatever a person sows, this he will also reap.

verses.rationale: Preserves agents, sources, and contrasting harvests.
verses.before: The one who sows to their own flesh will reap decay from the flesh, but the one who sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
verses.after: The one who sows for their own flesh will reap decay from the flesh, but the one who sows for the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the one who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption, but the one who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life.

verses.rationale: Keeps endurance and harvest promise.
verses.before: Let us not grow weary in doing good, because at the proper time we will reap if we do not give up.
verses.after: Let us not grow weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap if we do not give up.
verses.tsw_comparator: And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in due time we will reap, if we do not give up.

verses.rationale: Preserves universal good and special household care.
verses.before: So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to those who belong to the household of faith.
verses.after: Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us work for the good of everyone, and especially for those who belong to the household of faith.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all, and especially to those who are of the household of faith.

verses.rationale: Keeps visual size and personal handwriting.
verses.before: See what large letters I am writing to you with my own hand!
verses.after: See what large letters I write to you with my own hand!
verses.tsw_comparator: See with what large letters I am writing to you with my own hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily display, coercion, and motive.
verses.before: Those who want to make a good showing in the flesh are the ones trying to compel you to be circumcised, only so they will not be persecuted for Christ’s cross.
verses.after: Those who want to make a good showing in the flesh are the ones compelling you to be circumcised, only so that they will not be persecuted for Christ's cross.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is those who want to make a good showing in the flesh who compel you to be circumcised, and only so that they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps hypocrisy and bodily boasting.
verses.before: For even those who are circumcised do not themselves keep the Law, but they want you to be circumcised so they can boast in your flesh.
verses.after: For even those who are circumcised do not themselves keep the law, but they want you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: For even those who are circumcised do not themselves keep the law, but they want you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh.

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal crucifixion and sole boast.
verses.before: But may I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me and I to the world.
verses.after: But may I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me and I to the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily statuses and terse creation alternative.
verses.before: For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything; what matters is a new creation.
verses.after: For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything, but new creation is.
verses.tsw_comparator: For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything, but a new creation.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conjunction and distinct but debated referent.
verses.before: Peace and mercy upon all who walk by this rule, and upon the Israel of God.
verses.after: Peace and mercy be upon all who follow this rule, and upon the Israel of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as many as walk by this rule—peace be upon them and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily scars as marks of belonging.
verses.before: From now on let no one cause me trouble, because I carry the marks of Jesus on my body.
verses.after: From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I carry the marks of Jesus on my body.
verses.tsw_comparator: From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear in my body the marks of Jesus.

verses.rationale: Keeps grace, communal spirit, kinship, and Amen.
verses.before: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers and sisters. Amen.
verses.after: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers and sisters. Amen.
verses.tsw_comparator: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers and sisters. Amen.
